established_findings.statement: LLMs can produce draft network configurations or configuration-related code but frequently make syntax, topology, or semantic errors; pairing generation with deterministic verifiers or localized verification feedback measurably reduces those errors in prototype studies.
limitations: Evaluations are prototype-scale and task-limited (e.g., single-router translation, P4 device examples).
Human oversight still present in reported workflows; not full production deployment evidence.

established_findings.statement: Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) or verifier-grounded closed-loop architectures are a recurrent, empirically supported mitigation pattern for reducing mechanically verifiable errors in LLM outputs across domains (code, domain-specific programs, and configuration-like artifacts).
established_findings.evidence_type: method proposals with empirical single-case / domain studies
limitations: Effectiveness depends on existence of a suitable deterministic verifier/oracle and on the verifier providing localized, actionable feedback.
Reported results focus on mechanically checkable properties (compilation, formal semantics) rather than all semantic correctness modes.

established_findings.statement: Hallucination/confabulation in LLMs is a persistent phenomenon; detection and uncertainty-estimation techniques (semantic-entropy, multi-sample consistency) can identify many such failures but do not eliminate the underlying stochastic/coverage limitations.
established_findings.evidence_type: theoretical analyses and empirical detection studies
limitations: Detection methods identify subsets of hallucinations (e.g., confabulations) and have false positives/negatives.
Theoretical inevitability arguments are formal/idealized and do not prescribe practical elimination techniques.

established_findings.statement: Recent surveys and domain papers document rapid growth of LLM-for-NetOps / LLM-for-AIOps research but highlight recurring evaluation gaps: benchmark provenance, operational-validity of metrics, and limited realistic emulation/production testing.
limitations: Surveys synthesize available literature but themselves rely on the set of published studies (possible publication bias).
Specific gaps (e.g., dataset shortages) vary by subtask and are described at a high level rather than quantified uniformly.

unresolved_questions.statement: How well do verifier-assisted LLM workflows scale and generalize across heterogeneous, multi-vendor network environments, multi-device policies, and realistic operator workflows?
unresolved_questions.evidence_type: limited empirical prototypes and case studies
limitations: Existing studies show promise on narrow use cases (single-router translation, P4 examples) but do not provide broad cross-vendor or large-scale emulation evidence.

unresolved_questions.statement: To what extent can automated detection (semantic-entropy, consistency) and GVR loops prevent operationally consequential misconfigurations (policy violations causing outages/security breaches) in live or high-fidelity emulated NetOps settings?
limitations: Benchmarks and detection papers demonstrate effects on contained tasks; they do not measure end-to-end operational safety in production-grade testbeds.

unresolved_questions.statement: What standardized benchmarks, verifiers, and provenance practices are necessary to produce reproducible, operationally meaningful evaluations of LLM-based NetOps automation?
limitations: Existing calls-for-benchmarking identify needs but do not converge on a single standardized suite or verifier-interface for NetOps tasks.

candidate_gaps.statement: A gap exists in publicly available, provenance-traced NetOps datasets and verifier-integrated emulation experiments that pair realistic network state/topologies with deterministic or formal verifiers to quantify LLM failure modes.
limitations: NetConfEval and similar efforts provide initial benchmarks/prototypes but are not yet comprehensive or provenance-traced at scale.
Some domain-specific emulation resources exist (Mininet/GNS3 papers) but are not paired with standardized LLM+verifier pipelines publicly.

candidate_gaps.statement: Empirical quantification of types/frequencies of LLM-induced configuration faults (syntax, topology, policy violation, security misconfigurations) under realistic prompting, operator intent variability, and retry policies is limited.
limitations: Available studies report qualitative or small-sample quantitative results; comprehensive, statistically powered fault-mode catalogs tied to operational fault consequences are missing.

excluded_claims: LLMs (alone) are production-ready and safe for fully autonomous NetOps deployment without deterministic verification and human oversight.
Generate–Verify–Repair architectures completely eliminate hallucinations or make LLM outputs infallible for all semantic correctness classes.
This record set supports any claim of 'first' provenance for generating verifier-assisted NetOps workflows (no supplied record proves an uncontested first-in-field claim).
